findings.text: follow-on: complete() reports the withdrawal but leaves a surviving project-less pointer live. The early return at :4845-4846 fires before the promotion tail that unlinks the live pointer (promotion.py:7508) and calls _release_after_promotion, so for a run whose pointer exists and names no project, complete() returns status "withdrawn" while pointer_path(run_id) still exists. This review drove the author's own second case shape end to end against the committed content (scratch tree /tmp/rev-head-committed, whose run reports module_under_test /tmp/rev-head-committed/reckon/crew/promotion.py): after crew.complete returned withdrawn, the pointer was still present and classify_pointer read the run as "running" with next_action "reckon crew observe --run ...", and a second complete() would return withdrawn again without ever clearing it. The state thus contradicts the word complete() just reported: the plan's section-10 goal is that a run can always be reconciled from what survives, and a run that reads running forever after complete has not been reconciled. Outside this node's declared done-when (which asks only that completion report the withdrawal rather than fail validation), so it is recorded as a follow-on: a withdrawn run should also release its pointer and worktree, and a case should assert the pointer is gone. The pointerless shape - the one the fence's reported defect actually had - is unaffected, since there's no pointer to clear. Note for the coordinator: this run was resumed while the review ran (attempt 2, started 2026-10-02T07:30:39Z) and its worktree was observed being edited to rename the helper to _complete_withdrawn_run and add pointer retirement and workspace release around this same guard; the delivered commit dcd95ee5 reviewed here does not carry that change.

justifications.durability: The guard lives in product source and the covering test fails when it is reverted - reproduced by this review in a scratch copy, with the same two failing ids the manifest declares. The two cases drive the real crew.complete() entry point in an isolated RECKON_HOME, so the rule is exercised as production resolves it rather than against a private helper. The weaker point is that the withdrawal is reported but not made durable in observable state: for a surviving project-less pointer, complete() returns withdrawn while the pointer survives and the run keeps classifying as running (see the finding). No test asserts the pointer is cleared, so a regression that left every withdrawn pointer live would stay green.
justifications.evidence: Both arms are complete and readable. Base e89a94bde 55 passed EXIT=0 (logs/base-arm.log); head at the worktree content committed as dcd95ee15 55 passed EXIT=0 (logs/head-arm.log); failure_count 0 in both, so the manifest's added_failure_count of 0 is well-founded. The negative control is genuine: the declared mutation inserts ledger.ledger_path("", root) before the guard, and the red log shows EXIT=1 with two failing ids whose traceback is the project-name LedgerError (logs/negative-control.log). This review independently re-ran the new file against the committed content in a scratch tree (2 passed, EXIT=0; review-logs/review-head-rerun.log) and reproduced the declared mutation there (2 failed, EXIT=1, same LedgerError; review-logs/review-negative-control.log). Deducted for one provenance gap: head-arm.log omits the module_under_test and cwd header lines that base-arm.log carries, so the head run's imported module path and working directory are not stated on the log itself; the manifest's measurement_module names only the base-arm extraction, not the head run.
justifications.fit: _withdrawn_run_payload sits beside _read_pointer_or_rebuild, the helper owner it belongs to; it is a private module-level helper returning a plain dict shaped like complete()'s other payloads, so the new outcome is one branch rather than a parallel refusal family. The docstring states the mechanism (a dispatch refused before a project is resolved leaves an empty project; there is no ledger to hold a row) rather than the incident. No version suffixes, no plan or ticket identifiers in symbols, no AI attribution. Names read as what the code does.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The done-when the fence states - crew complete on a withdrawn run reports the withdrawal instead of failing project validation - is met. complete() (reckon/crew/promotion.py:4845-4846) detects the empty project immediately after _read_pointer_or_rebuild and returns _withdrawn_run_payload (promotion.py:4684) before any ledger load or gate check. The payload is a parsed JSON dict stating withdrawn true, status "withdrawn", project "", promoted false, ledger_row_written false, a reason, and the surviving record; no ledger row is written and no validation error is raised. Both shapes the fence names are covered: a pointerless run rebuilt from its run directory (the record carries rebuilt_from_run_directory true) and a surviving pointer that names no project. The reported defect was a pointerless run (r-20261001T230854840625-review-of-ctta-explanatory-figure); the pointer variant is the author's added case.
